payload.quote: As the backtesting sample size increases or the VaR confidence level declines the shape of the non-rejection area becomes “tighter” and more symmetric. This implies that if a user were to do either, the likelihood of experiencing a type II error would be lower.

payload.claim: Under a Normal P&L distribution assumption, the Kupiec-POF test is less likely to reject (fail) a VaR model that over-estimates volatility than one that under-estimates volatility by the same amount, and this asymmetry worsens as the VaR/test confidence interval increases or the backtesting sample size is reduced.
payload.quote: A simple visual inspection of these charts supports our previous expectation that the probability of experiencing a type II error is asymmetric around the correctly specified volatility. In particular, our results suggest that the Kupiec-POF test is in fact less likely to fail a VaR model which over-estimates volatility when compared to one that under-estimates volatility. Interestingly, this phenomenon worsens as the VaR/test confidence interval increases or the sample size is reduced.
